articles.title: 3 Takeaways From the Maple Leafs 2-1 Win Over the Islanders
articles.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs landed their first win of the season, 24 hours after dropping their season opener at home. The post 3 Takeaways From the Maple Leafs...
articles.body:
The Maple Leafs needed a response after Tuesday's disappointing opening-night loss to the Montreal Canadiens .

Toronto defeated the New York Islanders 2-1 on Wednesday night, getting goals from Colton Sissons and Easton Cowan before hanging on through a tense third period. The Maple Leafs were outshot by the Islanders 27-26 but, more importantly, looked considerably more structured defensively than they had 24 hours earlier.

A brutal defensive mistake in the third period allowed the Islanders to get on the board shorthanded, and suddenly what had looked like a comfortable two-goal lead became a one-goal game.

But the Maple Leafs found a way to close it out.

Here are three takeaways from Toronto's first win of the 2026-27 season.

Easton Cowan Looks Ready for a Bigger Role

Easton Cowan had the kind of game the Maple Leafs desperately needed from one of their young players.

He finished with two points, assisting on Sissons' opening goal before scoring Toronto's second goal on the power play.

The power-play goal was particularly important.

Cowan found himself in a dangerous position and made no mistake when the opportunity arrived, giving Toronto a 2-0 lead late in the first period.

His assist on Sissons' goal was just as encouraging. Cowan helped create the opening before Nick Paul and Sissons finished the play, giving him a hand in both of Toronto's goals.

That's exactly what the Maple Leafs need from him.

The trade of Matthew Knies to Columbus left Toronto with a much different-looking left side, and Cowan entered the season with an opportunity to take on a larger role. NHL.com had him projected on the third line against the Islanders, but his performance could force Jim Hiller to give him more responsibility sooner rather than later.

Cowan isn't going to suddenly become a 30-goal scorer because of one game.

But he is showing signs that he can become an important offensive piece for the Maple Leafs.

And Wednesday was a heck of a start. He earned the game's second star.

Anthony Stolarz Gives Toronto Exactly What It Needed

If Cowan provided the offense, Anthony Stolarz provided the insurance.

Stolarz stopped all 20 shots he faced before the Islanders finally broke through with a shorthanded goal in the third period.

That was the kind of performance the Maple Leafs needed after Tuesday.

Toronto's defensive execution was hardly flawless. There were still moments when the Islanders generated pressure, particularly as the game tightened in the third period.

The Maple Leafs turned the puck over in their own end while trying to move it up ice, with Darren Raddysh making the key misplay that ultimately allowed Emil Heineman to score shorthanded.

But it shouldn't overshadow what came before it.

Stolarz was excellent, and several of his saves kept the Islanders from turning Toronto's mistakes into goals. The Maple Leafs couldn't afford another night in which their goaltender was left fighting an uphill battle.

This time, Stolarz gave them the type of performance that allowed the rest of the team to survive its mistakes.

The Maple Leafs Penalty Kill Was Outstanding

The Maple Leafs also deserve plenty of credit for what they did when they went shorthanded.

Toronto killed off both Islanders power plays, keeping New York off the scoreboard on the man advantage.

That might not sound particularly dramatic, but it became increasingly important as the game progressed.

The Maple Leafs had a two-goal lead for most of the night. Every penalty created another opportunity for the Islanders to change the momentum.

That is a significant improvement from the type of defensive performance the team wanted to clean up after Tuesday's loss. The Maple Leafs were more willing to block shots, clear rebounds and make the simple play when they needed to.

They finished with 16 blocked shots compared to 11 for New York, another indication that the defensive effort was considerably more committed.

The shorthanded goal was certainly a blemish.

But outside of that one disastrous sequence, the Maple Leafs did what they needed to do.

They got timely scoring from Cowan, a brilliant performance from Stolarz and a perfect night from the penalty kill.

After opening the season with a loss, that's exactly the kind of bounce-back performance Toronto needed.

articles.title: Michigan football news: John Henry Daley, Andrew Marsh on injury report
articles.summary: Michigan football enters its next Big Ten test with several important health questions hanging over the Wolverines. As Michigan prepares for a matchup with M...
articles.body:
Michigan football enters its next Big Ten test with several important health questions hanging over the Wolverines . As Michigan prepares for a matchup with Minnesota , John Henry Daley and Andrew Marsh headline a loaded injury report. That could significantly influence the team's approach Saturday.

Daley is Michigan's leading edge rusher with three sacks and 11 pressures. He is listed as questionable after suffering a lower-body injury late in the Wolverines' loss to Iowa . The encouraging development is that Daley has been walking without a boot or crutches. His availability would provide a major boost to a Michigan defense preparing for another conference challenge.

Marsh, meanwhile, is also questionable. That leaves another key offensive piece uncertain heading into the weekend. Marsh leads the team with 22 catches for a total of receiving 239 yards so far. The Wolverines are additionally monitoring edge rusher Dom Nichols and offensive lineman Andrew Sprague. They both carry 'questionable' designations. There is better news along the offensive line, with Blake Frazier listed as probable and trending toward availability.

Michigan enters the matchup at 3–1 overall and 0–1 in Big Ten play under head coach Kyle Whittingham. The Wolverines opened with a 13–12 win over Western Michigan . They stunned No. 11 Oklahoma 17–10 and cruised past UTEP 52–17. That was before suffering a narrow 20–19 home loss to No. 17 Iowa . Quarterback Bryce Underwood and wide receiver JJ Buchanan lead their offense. Now, Michigan needs a bounce-back performance against Minnesota. Getting its questionable contributors cleared could be critical as the Wolverines look to reclaim momentum and strengthen their conference standing.

articles.title: Recap: Opening night mayhem leads to 8-4 Avalanche win
articles.summary: The power play giveth and the power play taketh.
articles.body:
For the first game out of 84 in the 2026-27 season the Colorado Avalanche hosted the LA Kings at Ball Arena and it won't soon be forgotten. A 8-4 rout of the Kings saw multiple power play and shorthanded goals against for Colorado and even a Nathan MacKinnon fight.

Believe it or not but the power play got the Avalanche on the board first, however in pure hilarious fashion it was the second unit that got the job done. Brock Nelson deflected a rebound off of Kings goaltender Darcy Kuemper 's mask and into the net. The Kings then got their own power play and didn't score on it but seemed to give them momentum. After a couple big saves from Mackenzie Blackwood and good pings, Los Angeles finally broke through. It was defenseman Brian Dumoulin who got a shot through traffic to even the score. The next Kings power play didn't go well either but Parker Kelly got a strike on a breakaway just after the penalty expired to put Colorado up by one heading into the first intermission.

A five-on-three for Colorado carried over into the second frane and the boys in burgundy made it count as Nathan MacKinnon lit the lamp just 23 seconds into the period. Just one minute later, though, Joel Armia got one back for the Kings shorthanded when he beat Blackwood from distance. At 3-2 was the closest the Kings got because the Avalanche added two more scores in the second period. First, again from MacKinnon and then Nic Roy. On the latter goal Jaden Schwartz was lying open the crease making contact with Kuemper but the Kings didn't even try to challenge the goal so Colorado was up 5-3 at that point.

But, not so fast. Los Angeles got their second shorthanded goal of the period when Trevor Moore put a snipe on Blackwood. The Avalanche responded when the second power play unit was put back on the ice to finish out the man advantage and Artturi Lehkonen converted from the slot. So the Avalanche were back up by three with a 6-3 score going into the second intermission.

On a particularly bad shift for Josh Manson halfway through the third period where he lost the puck leading to extended offensive zone time for Los Angeles and then took a penalty, it was Artemi Panarin who scored from distance through traffic on the delayed penalty to put the fourth Kings goal on the board.

If ten goals wasn't exciting enough, there was a Nathan MacKinnon fight against Kings defenseman Brandt Clarke . The Avalanche superstar was the instigator and even landed a few rights in the process. There was still ten minutes to go after the brawl and Gabe Landeskog scored his first goal of the season on rebound after Cale Makar drove to the net. For the eighth and final tally Lehkonen got another power play goal with the second unit and the game finally arrived at a 8-4 Avalanche final.

There was just about everything in this game from good and bad goaltending, power play goals galore and even a couple shorties. It showed the sloppy nature of this game that counted for the first time in September in Avalanche history. There will be a lot of days off this month to tighten up some mistakes and mishaps while building on early successes.

Special teams were certainly special this evening. On one hand the Avalanche got four power play goals, yet gave up two shorthanded. The first unit only converted on a five-on-three and the second unit carried the load with a trio of their own. Two functional power play groups would be ideal but how long is it going to last before just heavily favoring the first unit again?

One more game at home against the St. Louis Blues starting at 7 p.m. MT on Saturday, October 3rd.

articles.title: What punishment do rival Premier League clubs want for Manchester City?
articles.summary: A number of Premier League clubs believe a points deduction that would relegate Manchester City to the Championship for one season would be insufficient.Give...
articles.body:
A number of Premier League clubs believe a points deduction that would relegate Manchester City to the Championship for one season would be insufficient.

Given the scale of City's offences, these clubs want a sanction that will result in a prolonged absence from the English top-flight ( The Guardian ).

The independent commission that found them guilty of the rule breaches will determine their punishment at a sanctions hearing.

The Citizens have confirmed they will appeal against the damning findings.

The appeal hearing, per the league's new rules, must be concluded within 12 weeks of being filed.

But City could delay the process by arguing the new rules should not apply as they were introduced this season while the charges against them are historic.

Man City have dominated English football since Sheikh Mansoor's takeover in 2008, winning 22 major trophies including eight Premier League titles and a Champions League.

But now their reputation is on the line after being found guilty of all charges related to breaches of financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

If their appeal fails, the club could be fined, docked points or even expelled from the competition altogether.

articles.title: Liverpool told what it will take to sign 'outstanding' star from arch-rivals
articles.summary: Liverpool are currently sixth in the Premier League. This means that, at the moment, they're sitting outside of the Champions League spots which is far from...
articles.body:
Liverpool are currently sixth in the Premier League.

This means that, at the moment, they're sitting outside of the Champions League spots which is far from ideal.

Last term, Arne Slot led his men to a fifth-place finish and, in a normal campaign, qualifying for Europe's premium competition would have been the bare minimum but, just a season after winning the Premier League title, fans wanted to see their team at least try and defend it.

This obviously didn't end up happening which is why Slot was relieved of his duties and why Liverpool had to spend another £150 million on new players.

Andoni Iraola was the man chosen to take over and, while his impact on the squad has been fairly impressive, more can come from the Anfield outfit.

And, at the moment, fans need more so that they know that their club are going to be able to handle themselves by the end of the term.

However, since their squad depth is so thin, it's unclear whether they'll make it all the way to the end or not which is why transfers are already being mooted in January.

Everton want £80 million for Jarrad Branthwaite

Even though Liverpool focused on improving their defence in the summer, some cracks are still showing.

Jeremy Jacquet , Virgil van Dijk and Ronald Araujo have all helped shore up the Reds' back line massively and, without this trio among their ranks, Liverpool would be so much worse off.

However, left-back is a different story altogether with neither Kostas Tsimikas nor Milos Kerkez meeting the standards expected of them.

But, since Van Dijk 's current Liverpool contract is set to expire in June 2027, his future is undecided.

And, while Liverpool's fans will almost certainly want the Dutchman to stay, it does feel like Liverpool will need to have a succession plan in place just in case their captain doesn't stay on.

That's why this latest update from Football Insider on Everton's valuation of Jarrad Branthwaite will certainly pique the interest of Liverpool's fanbase.

"Everton still believe that centre-back Jarrad Branthwaite is an £80million player, sources have told Football Insider," they wrote .

"The Toffees have no plans to cash in on the 24-year-old, and still regard him as one of the Premier League's best defenders when he is fit.

"Sources say that while the Merseysiders do not want to lose the defender, they are confident that he will net them an eye-watering sum one day.

"Former Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider last week that Liverpool are working on a shock move to sign Branthwaite next summer.

"The ex-recruitment chief outlined that the Reds have had scouts watching the defender at the Hill Dickinson S tad ium on several occasions of late.

"Brown made it clear that Liverpool are doing their "due diligence" on Branthwaite, and believe he "ticks a lot of boxes" as a potential replacement for Virgil van Dijk."

Liverpool signing Jarrad Branthwaite would be unreal for them

One thing that rarely ever happens is Liverpool and Everton conducting transfer business with one another.

Although both teams are often at opposite ends of the Premier League table to one another, their rivalry is still fierce with both sets of fans looking forward to their fixtures each season.

And, even though a deal for Ndiaye is now off the table thanks to him joining Manchester City , a deal for the English centre-back could certainly brighten the mood at Anfield if Van Dijk chooses to exit.

Indeed, the " outstanding " defender's injury history is a tad worrying but, since he's managed to stay fit since the start of the 2026-27 season, there's hope that he's now grown out of that stage in his career.

Branthwaite is still only 24 years old so he has plenty of time to grow into an even better player and, if he's wanting to challenge for silverware and not move too far away from his current home, where better is there for him to go than L4?

Here's hoping that these rumours are true and Liverpool actually try and agree a deal with their rivals for him.

articles.title: Bears news: Chicago's LT situation murky again with new injury update
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears secured a dominant 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football, but the win came with a troubling setback along the...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears secured a dominant 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football, but the win came with a troubling setback along the offensive line. Starting left tackle Braxton Jones exited the contest with a knee injury, and head coach Ben Johnson confirmed that Jones is now considered week-to-week.

Jones played a pivotal role in Chicago's impressive 2-1 start to the 2026 regular season, providing steady protection on the perimeter. Before his departure, the Bears offense executed efficiently against Philadelphia's defensive front, accumulating 375 total net yards and holding the ball for nearly 37 minutes. Losing Jones creates a glaring hole on the blind side right as Chicago prepares for a Week 4 matchup against the New York Jets .

Filling that vacancy is not a simple task. Offensive tackle Ozzy Trapilo continues working his way back from his own injury, but his status for Sunday remains up in the air. Addressing Trapilo's timeline, Johnson admitted that the blocker is "getting closer," though he cautioned, "I don't know if this will be the week or not."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

If Trapilo cannot play, Chicago must get creative with its front five. Johnson mentioned that guard Jordan McFadden can play tackle if needed, along with veteran guard Joe Thuney . Backup tackle Theo Benedet stepped in for 17 snaps after Jones went down, but reshuffling position assignments on short notice poses a real test for unit chemistry.

Chicago's offense found plenty of rhythm against Philadelphia, tallying 128 rushing yards led by running back D'Andre Swift's 84-yard performance while quarterback Case Keenum threw for a touchdown. Still, losing Jones forces Johnson into immediate contingency planning. Whether Trapilo returns, McFadden slides outside, or Benedet gets the nod, Chicago must lock down the left tackle spot quickly to keep its offensive momentum intact.

articles.title: Can India, Pakistan be in same group at ODI World Cup 2027? Explaining how World Cup draw is made
articles.summary: How the 2027 ODI World Cup draw will determine whether India and Pakistan are placed in the same group.
articles.body:
The ICC Men's ODI World Cup 2027 features a new format where 14 teams will take part in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.

However, contrary to the last two editions, the ODI World Cup will not start with all participating teams meeting in one league.

The 14 teams will be divided into two groups according to their ranking, before the tournament proceeds into the two-group phase and Super 7.

But it raises a big question for fans - will India and Pakistan play in the same group at 2027 ODI World Cup?

Reports indicate that India and Pakistan may play in the same group in the upcoming World Cup but no official confirmation has been revealed by sources prior to the October 1 announcement of the schedule.

The Sporting News explores how the 2027 World Cup draw will be conducted and whether India and Pakistan will play in the same group.

The 2027 ODI World Cup will consist of 14 teams, although only 12 will qualify directly to the main group stage.

The three lowest-ranked teams out of the 14 qualifying teams will first compete in a three-team Super Series, where each team will face the other two in one match. The winning team will move on to the main stage, while the other two will be knocked out.

The remaining 11 teams along with the winner of the Super Series will thus make up the 12-team main stage.

These 12 teams will be split into two groups of six each, where each team plays five matches against the others in their group. The top three in each group, along with the best fourth-placed team out of the two groups, will make up the Super 7.

When will the ODI World Cup 2027 groups be announced?

The ICC will announce the groups and schedule for the 2027 ODI World Cup on October 1, 2026, with the draw being held in Cape Town at 8:30 p.m. IST.

The draw results will also reveal whether or not India and Pakistan are in the same group.

The 2027 ODI World Cup draw will determine the groups, venues and match dates, with the ICC and Cricket South Africa unveiling the complete fixture list at the Cape Town event on October 1.

The draw comes after the September 30 ODI rankings cut-off, which determines the directly qualified teams. The final group allocation done at random will establish which teams are placed together in the two Round 2 groups.

The 12 teams in Round 2 will be divided into two groups of six each.

The ICC confirmed the group structure but there is no indication whether the allocation will be completely random or use rankings, seeding or predetermined pots.

Therefore, the September 30 ODI rankings should not automatically be interpreted as a seeding order for the Round 2 draw. The official schedule and group announcement on October 1 is expected to provide clarity on how the 12 teams are allocated between the two groups.

Can India, Pakistan be in same group at ODI World Cup 2027?

This all depends on how they will be grouped in the end.

India and Pakistan were drawn in the same group at the last two ODI World Cups, in 2019 and 2023. They also met in the group stage in 2015, while their 2011 meeting was in the semi-finals.

Both nations have qualified for the 2027 World Cup through the ODI rankings and will not play in the Super Series.

Reports stating that India and Pakistan are set to be grouped together in one six-nation group are not officially confirmed as of yet and will only be confirmed when ICC announces the schedule.

If the two teams are indeed grouped together in one group, they will certainly face each other at least once in the group stage itself.

How many times can India play Pakistan at 2027 World Cup?

The new format presents the prospect of up to three India-Pakistan encounters at the 2027 World Cup.

In case the two teams are grouped together and both manage to reach the Super 7 stage, they will get the opportunity to encounter each other during that stage since all the seven teams in the Super 7 stage play against one another.

A third encounter can take place in either the semi-finals or final stages, depending on how the two teams place themselves in the Super 7 rankings. Four teams move forward to the semi-finals; first plays fourth and second plays third.

However, in case they are placed in separate groups, they won't be able to encounter each other in the group stage. They will still have the chance of meeting each other either in the Super 7 stage or in the knockout stage if they both qualify.

Where to watch the 2027 ODI World Cup draw in India

The Star Sports Network will broadcast the World Cup 2027 draw live and it can be live-streamed on JioHotstar app and website.
